BURSEVI:v5p155/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p155/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p155/r4.claim: The exception is connected: God may have mercy and return the Qur'an, with mercy personified as an advocate for its restoration.
BURSEVI:v5p155/r4.anchor: إلا أن يرحمك ربك فيرد عليك كأن رحمته تتوكل عليك بالرد فالاستثناء متصل

BURSEVI:v5p155/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p155/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p155/r5.claim: Alternatively, the exception is disconnected: mercy from the Lord is that He leaves the Qur'an preserved and does not erase it.
BURSEVI:v5p155/r5.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (ليكن رحمتست از روردكار توكه آنرا باقي

BURSEVI:v5p155/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p155/r6.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v5p155/r6.claim: “Except as mercy” can be a purpose complement: God preserved the revelation for mercy; although addressed to the Prophet, the warning concerns others.
BURSEVI:v5p155/r6.anchor: وفي "الكواشي" إلا رحمة مفعول له أي : حفظناه عليك

BURSEVI:v5p155/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p155/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p155/r7.claim: God's great favor to Muhammad consists in sending him, revealing the Book, preserving it in his memory, and making him the Seal of the Prophets.
BURSEVI:v5p155/r7.anchor: بإرسالك وإنزال الكتاب عليك وإبقائه في حفظك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r1.speaker: ابن الأنباري وابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r1.claim: They parse except as an unrelated exception meaning 'but', correcting the prior conditional claim that God might take away the Quran.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r1.anchor: استثناء منقطع على ما اختاره ابن الأنباري وابن عطية وغيرهما

ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r2.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r2.claim: Al-Kashf says the exception corrects 'no advocate': after the Quran is taken away, no one could restore it, but God's mercy preserved it; this is grammatically a disconnected exception.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r2.anchor: فإن المستثنى منه ( وكيلا ) وهذا من المنقطع الممتنع إيقاعه موقع الاسم الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r3.claim: Another parse makes mercy a connected exception from advocate, so mercy itself serves as the guarantor of retrieval; Al-Alusi says this strains the word advocate.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r3.anchor: اختيار أنه استثناء متصل من ( وكيلا ) أي لا تجد وكيلا باسترداده إلا الرحمة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa parses mercy as an accusative purpose, meaning God preserved the Quran for mercy, or as an absolute object meaning God showed mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء : إن ( رحمة ) نصب على أنه مفعول له والتقدير حفظناه عليك للرحمة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r5.claim: On the disconnected reading, the verse favors the Prophet by preserving the Quran after favoring him with its revelation; the connected reading would make the favor only its original revelation and seems obscure.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r5.anchor: والآية على تقدير الانقطاع امتنان بإبقاء القرآن بعد الإمتنان بتنزيله

ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r6.claim: The verse appears to describe removal as merely hypothetical and mercy as the reason no recovery-agent would be needed, yet reports say the Quran will later be removed before the Hour.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r6.anchor: والآية ظاهرة في أن مشيئة الذهاب به غير متحققة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r7.speaker: حذيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r7.claim: A strong report, authenticated by al-Hakim, says Islam will fade, the Quran will be lifted in one night with no verse left on earth, and only elderly people will retain the declaration of God's oneness.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r7.anchor: عن حذيفة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : يدرس الإسلام كما يدرس وشى الثوب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r8.claim: They report the Prophet warning against writings alongside the Quran: God may remove every Quranic letter from paper and hearts overnight, while people favored with good retain لا إله إلا الله.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس وابن عمر قالا : خطب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : يا أيها الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r9.claim: A report authenticated by al-Hakim says the Quran and other revealed books will be lifted to heaven, leaving no verses or guidance in people's hearts.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164#2/r9.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : يسري على كتاب الله تعالى فيرفع إلى السماء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r1.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says that before the Hour the Quran will return to its source, buzzing around the Throne and declaring it came from God and returns to Him, recited but not obeyed.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r1.anchor: لا تقوم الساعة حتى يرجع القرآن من حيث جاء له دوي حول العرش

ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Nasr transmits a similar report attributed to Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r2.anchor: وأخرج محمد بن نصر نحوه مرفوعا على عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص

ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r3.claim: Several transmitters report Ibn Masud saying the Quran will be lifted from manuscripts and memories, after which he recited this verse; al-Bahja says removal from manuscripts comes first.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r3.anchor: وأخرج غير واحد عن ابن مسعود أنه قال : سيرفع القرآن من المصاحف والصدور ثم قرأ

ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r4.speaker: ابن أبي حاتم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r4.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits that Gabriel will take the Quran away.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r4.anchor: والذاهب به هو جبريل عليه السلام كما أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r5.claim: If the verse predicts taking the Quran away, these reports agree with it; if it promises preservation, the conflict can be resolved by saying preservation lasts until shortly before the Hour.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r5.anchor: فإن دلت الآية على الذهاب به فلا منافاة بينها وبين هذه الأخبار

ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r6.claim: The context signals favor: God's great favor includes revealing the Quran, choosing the Prophet above creation, making him the final prophet, and granting him the praised station.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r6.anchor: ومنه إنزال القرآن واصطفاؤه على جميع الخلق وختم الأنبياء عليهم السلام به

ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r7.speaker: أبو سهل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r7.claim: Abu Sahl says the verse threatens other people with losing what they received, discouraging questions about withheld knowledge such as the spirit or the Hour.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r7.anchor: إلى أنها سقيت لتهديد غيره صلى الله عليه وسلم بإذهاب ما أوتوا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r8.speaker: صاحب التحرير
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r8.claim: The author of al-Tahrir suggests the delayed revelation about the spirit, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the People of the Cave distressed the Prophet, and this verse comforted him by reminding him God could remove all revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r8.anchor: لما سئل عن الروح وذي القرنين وأهل الكهف وأبطأ عليه الوحي شق عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p165/r9.claim: Al-Alusi dismisses both Abu Sahl's threat interpretation and al-Tahrir's consolation interpretation as unpersuasive.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p127/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p127/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p127/r1.claim: The exception is disconnected: God will not remove the Qur'an, but by mercy from Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p127/r1.anchor: {إلا رحمة من ربك} هذا استثناء منقطع معناه: ولكن (1) لا نشاء ذلك رحمة من ربك.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p127/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p127/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p127/r2.claim: The threatened removal means erasing the Qur'an from manuscripts and from people's hearts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p127/r2.anchor: المراد منه: محوه من المصاحف وإذهاب ما في الصدور.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p127/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p127/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p127/r3.claim: Ibn Masud urges people to recite before the Qur'an is raised; a report says it will disappear from books and hearts overnight, leaving people to recite poetry.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p127/r3.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود: اقرؤوا القرآن قبل أن يرفع فإنه لا تقوم الساعة حتى يرفع.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p127/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p127/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p127/r4.claim: Ibn Amr says the Qur'an will return to its place of descent, humming around the Throne like bees because people recited but did not act on it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p127/r4.anchor: لا تقوم الساعة حتى يرجع القرآن من حيث نزل له دوي حول العرش كدوي النحل

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:86-88/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:86-88/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:86-88/r3.claim: The exception may mean that if the Lord's mercy reaches him, He may restore the Qur'an; alternatively, it is disconnected—'but for mercy'—thanking God for retaining it after revealing it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:86-88/r3.anchor: إلا رحمة من ربك } فإنها إن نالتك فلعلهما تسترده عليك، ويجوز أن يكون استثناء منقطعا بمعنى ولكن رحمة من ربك تركته غير مذهوب به، فيكون امتنانا بإبقائه بعد المنة في تنزيله.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:86-88/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:86-88/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:86-88/r4.claim: God's great favor to the Prophet includes sending him and revealing the Book, then preserving it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:86-88/r4.anchor: إن فضله كان عليك كبيرا } كإرساله وإنزال الكتاب عليه وإبقائه في حفظه.

QASHANI:17:85-87/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:85-87/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:85-87/r4.claim: Only a special, immense mercy protects the Prophet: the mercy of the Merciful grants him complete perfection and sustains his existence and revelation.
QASHANI:17:85-87/r4.anchor: مجرد رحمة عظيمة خاصة بك من فرط عنايتنا وهي أعلى مراتب الرحمة الرحيمية

QASHANI:17:85-87/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:85-87/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:85-87/r5.claim: A direct manifestation of the divine essence would leave neither revelation nor the Prophet's self; manifestation through mercy brings both into being, while majesty can veil revelation and knowledge.
QASHANI:17:85-87/r5.anchor: لو تجلينا بذاتنا لما وجدت الوحي ولا ذاتك إلا إذا تجلينا بصفة الرحمة

QASHANI:17:85-87/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:85-87/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:85-87/r6.claim: The great favor is eternal: revelation and divine teaching came after the gift of necessary existence.
QASHANI:17:85-87/r6.anchor: بالإيحاء والتعليم الرباني بعد موهبة الوجود الحقاني

BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r4.claim: The continued gift of revelation is an immense favor to the Prophet and his community, so the verse strongly emphasizes its greatness.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r4.anchor: ولما كان في إنزاله إليه ثم إبقائه لديه من النعمة عليه وعلى أمته ما لا يحصى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r5.claim: A report says the Qur’an will disappear at the end of time from both written copies and people’s hearts; the author says this verse implies that possibility.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r5.anchor: وقد ورد أنه يذهب بالقرآن في آخر الزمان , يسري بما في المصاحف وبما في القلوبن وقد أفهمت ذلك هذه الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r1.claim: The warning follows the Quran’s healing and mercy: knowledge should prompt gratitude, not conceit, since God can withdraw it; this cautions the Prophet and, by extension, other scholars.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r1.anchor: أعقب ذلك بالتنبيه إلى الشكر على نعمة العلم دفعا لغرور النفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r2.claim: The statement explicitly warns of removal but indirectly expresses favor, as the next verse explains; the Prophet is addressed because his knowledge is greatest.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r2.anchor: فالكلام صريحه تحذير ، وهو كناية عن الامتنان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p201/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p201/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p201/r1.claim: وكيل is used here for an advocate seeking restoration of a withdrawn favor, whereas نصير in the preceding warning concerns defending against punishment or avenging its recipient.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p201/r1.anchor: وذكر هنا { وكيلا } وفي الآية قبلها { نصيرا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p201/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p201/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p201/r2.claim: إلا رحمة من ربك is a disconnected exception functioning as a qualification: divine mercy in fact prevented the hypothetical removal of revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p201/r2.anchor: والاستثناء في قوله : { إلا رحمة من ربك } منقطع فحرف الاستثناء فيه بمعنى الاستدراك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p201/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p201/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p201/r3.claim: The passage hints at the Qur'an’s preservation, as affirmed in the verse that says God guards the Reminder.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p201/r3.anchor: وهذا إيماء إلى بقاء القرآن وحفظه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p201/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p201/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p201/r4.claim: The following clause explains why mercy prevented removal: God’s favor to the Prophet was great; كان and the emphatic particle reinforce the explanation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p201/r4.anchor: وموقع إن فضله كان عليك كبيرا } موقع التعليل للاستثناء المنقطع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r1.claim: Except as mercy is a disconnected exception meaning but a mercy from your Lord preserves it; unlike a connected exception, it specifies something outside the same category.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r1.anchor: وقوله إلا رحمة استثناء منقطع، أي لكن رحمة من ربك تمسك ذلك عليك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p483/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p483/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p483/r1.claim: God counts His great favor in granting the Prophet prophethood and protecting him from polytheists.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p483/r1.anchor: ثم عدد عليه عز وجل كبر فضله في اختصاصه بالنبوة وحمايته من المشركين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p483/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p483/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p483/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says only an outsider would deny disconnected exceptions in the Qurʾān, noting a view attributed to Ibn Khuwayz Mindad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p483/r9.anchor: ولا ينكر وقوع المنقطع في القرآن إلا أعجمي، وقد حكي ذلك عن ابن خويز منداد

JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r7.claim: Rahmatan is accusative as a verbal noun, meaning God had mercy.
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r7.anchor: رحمة نصب على المصدر؛ أي: رحم رحمة.

JISHUMI:v6p4294/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r9.claim: The exception means the Qur'an's descent and preservation are a mercy from God and a great favor to the Prophet.
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r9.anchor: إلا رحمة من ربك أي: لكن ذلك من رحمة ربك، أي: أنزله عليك وحفظه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p646/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p646/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p646/r2.claim: Except for God's mercy may be a disconnected exception, meaning that His mercy left the Qur'an with the Prophet rather than removing it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p646/r2.anchor: أو يكون على الاستثناء المنقطع بمعنى : ولكن رحمة من ربك تركته غير مذهوب به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p646/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p646/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p646/r3.claim: The Qur'an's continued preservation follows God's immense favor in revealing and teaching it; scholars should be grateful both for learning that remains in memory and for its continued preservation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p646/r3.anchor: وهذا امتنان من الله تعالى ببقاء القرآن محفوظا بعد المنة العظيمة في تنزيله وتحفيظه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p646/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p646/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p646/r4.claim: Ibn Masud foretells that trust will be the first religious quality lost, prayer the last, and a time when people pray without religion and the Qur'an disappears.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p646/r4.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود : : أول ما تفقدون من دينكم الأمانة ، وآخر ما تفقدون الصلاة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p646/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p646/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p646/r5.claim: In response to how the Qur'an could disappear after preservation in hearts and manuscripts and teaching children, Ibn Masud says it will be lifted overnight from manuscripts and hearts.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p646/r5.anchor: فقال : يسرى عليه ليلا فيصبح الناس منه فقراء ترفع المصاحف وينزع ما في القلوب

FARRA:v2p129/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p129/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p129/r9.claim: إلا رحمة من ربك is a disconnected exception, like the exception of Jacob’s need.
FARRA:v2p129/r9.anchor: وقوله: إلا رحمة من ربك [87] استثناء كقوله (إلا حاجة في نفس يعقوب قضاها) .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r5.claim: God’s mercy preserved Muhammad and kept the revelation with him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r5.anchor: أي لكن رحمة من ربك أبقاك له وأبقاه عليك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r6.claim: God’s favor was great either because it was abundant or because its significance was immense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r6.anchor: أحدهما : جزيلا لكثرته . الثاني : جليلا لعظيم خطره .

MUQATIL:17:85-87/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r6.claim: The exception is God's mercy: the Qur'an was specially granted to the Prophet, and God's favor was immense.
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r6.anchor: يعني القرآن كان رحمة من ربك اختصك بها، { إن فضله كان عليك كبيرا } [آية: 87]

NASAFI-FULL:v2p299/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p299/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p299/r1.claim: The exception may mean that God mercifully returns the Qurʾān, as if His mercy acts as its guardian, or it may be disconnected: His mercy left it unerased. Its preservation is a great favor and answers al-Naḍr's boast that he could produce its like.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p299/r1.anchor: إلا أن يرحمك ربك فيرده عليك كأن رحمته تتوكل عليه بالرد أو يكون على الاستثناء المنقطع

RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r5.claim: Except by mercy means either that God may mercifully return the revelation, or, as a disconnected exception, that His mercy left it unerased; its preservation is divine favor.
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r5.anchor: إلا أن يرحمك ربك فيرده عليك أو يكون على الاستثناء المنقطع

RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r6.claim: God's favor to scholars includes two gifts: making knowledge accessible and preserving it in them.

RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r7.claim: One interpretation says God's great favor is preserving knowledge and Quran for the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r7.anchor: المراد أن فضله كان عليك كبيرا بسبب إبقاء العلم والقرآن عليك

RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r8.claim: A second interpretation locates the great favor in making Muhammad master of Adam's children, the seal of prophets, and possessor of the Praiseworthy Station.
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r8.anchor: جعلك سيد ولد آدم وختم بك النبيين وأعطاك المقام المحمود

NAHHAS:v2p439/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p439/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p439/r3.claim: The exception is detached from what came before: unless God shows mercy and restores that knowledge; divine mercy is gracious favor.
NAHHAS:v2p439/r3.anchor: استثناء ليس من الأول أي إلا أن يرحمك الله فيرد اليك ذلك

STUDYQURAN:17:86/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r1.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r1.claim: Although the verses use singular address, verse 86 is read as addressing everyone or the Prophet and community, while the final sentence of verse 87 is addressed to the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r1.anchor: most commentators read v. 86 as addressed to people in general

STUDYQURAN:17:86/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r2.claim: The Prophet's great bounty is his excellence among humans and his status as the seal of the prophets.
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r2.anchor: in it Bounty refers to his station of excellence among human beings

STUDYQURAN:17:86/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r8.claim: These warning and exception express God's mercy in revealing and preserving the Quran in people's hearts and writing; mercy and bounty are paired elsewhere.
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r8.anchor: Both the warning and the exception indicate that God’s Mercy is manifested not only in revealing the Quran

TAB-FULL:v15p75/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p75/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p75/r1.claim: God preserves the revelation by mercy and favor; the favor includes choosing Muhammad for the message and sending countless revelations.

TABATABAI:17:86-89/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:86-89/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:86-89/r2.claim: ‘Except as a mercy’ supplies an ellipsis: the Prophet received and retained the Spirit only by his Lord's mercy, whose favor upon him was great.
TABATABAI:17:86-89/r2.anchor: استثناء من محذوف يدل عليه السياق

TABRISI:17:85/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:85/r2.claim: In verse 87, mercy is an exception from the preceding statement: God preserved revelation in the Prophet’s heart; the oath’s answer governs yaʾtūn.
TABRISI:17:85/r2.anchor: إلا رحمة من ربك الرحمة استثناء من الأول والمعنى ولكن الله تعالى رحمك

TABRISI:17:85-87/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85-87/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:85-87/r13.claim: The exception means God’s mercy gave the Prophet knowledge, withheld other matters, and established the Qurʾān in his and believers’ hearts; this immense favor calls for gratitude.
TABRISI:17:85-87/r13.anchor: لكن رحمة من الله ربك لك أعطاك ما أعطاك من العلوم ومنعك

TABRISI:17:85-87/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85-87/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:17:85-87/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains God’s great favor as making the Prophet leader of humanity, seal of prophets, and recipient of the praised station.
TABRISI:17:85-87/r14.anchor: حيث جعلك سيد ولد آدم وختم ربك النبيين وأعطاك المقام المحمود

THALABI:v6p130#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p130#2/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p130#2/r11.claim: The exception means God refrains from taking the revelation through mercy; His favor to the Prophet is great.
THALABI:v6p130#2/r11.anchor: إلا رحمة من ربك يعني لكن لا يشاء ربك رحمة من ذلك، إن فضله كان عليك كبيرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p472/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p472/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p472/r1.claim: He takes illa raḥmatan as an exception, comparable to the exception in Joseph 12:68.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p472/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: هو استثناء، كقوله: {إلا حاجة في نفس يعقوب}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p472/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p472/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p472/r2.claim: The exception is disconnected: God instead showed mercy by fixing the revelation in the Prophet's and believers' hearts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p472/r2.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: {رحمت} استثناء ليس من الأول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p472/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p472/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p472/r3.claim: God's great favor was making Muhammad master of Adam's descendants, the seal of prophets, and giver of the Praiseworthy Station.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p472/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد حيث جعلتك سيد ولد آدم،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:87-89/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:87-89/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:87-89/r1.claim: God had mercy on the Prophet by fixing revelation in his heart and believers' hearts; His great favor made Muhammad master of Adam's descendants and granted him the praised station.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:87-89/r1.anchor: لكن الله رحمك فأثبت ذلك في قلبك وقلوب المؤمنين { إن فضله كان عليك كبيرا } حيث جعلك سيد ولد آدم، وأعطاك المقام المحمود.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161#2/r1.claim: The verse has an implied phrase: God sent the Qur’an down to the Prophet only as mercy from Him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161#2/r1.anchor: إلا رحمة من ربك} [الإسراء: 87] فيها إضمار، يقول: وإنما أنزلناه عليك رحمة من ربك.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161#2/r2.claim: God’s great favor to the Prophet was granting prophethood and revealing the Qur’an.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161#2/r2.anchor: إن فضله كان عليك كبيرا} [الإسراء: 87] يقول: أعطاك النبوة وأنزل عليك القرآن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161#2/r3.claim: Ibn Masud says the Qur’an will be removed in a single night from every heart and copy, leaving no verse.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161#2/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: ليسرين على القرآن ليلة، فلا تبقى منه آية في قلب رجل ولا مصحف

ELMALILI:17:86-87/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:86-87/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:86-87/r2.claim: Except for mercy from the Lord, the Prophet can rely on no one; the same Lord who revealed the Qur’an preserves it and sustains him through a special grace meant to spread universal mercy.
ELMALILI:17:86-87/r2.anchor: ancak Rabbinden bir rahmet evvel ü âhir yalnız O’na dayanabilirsin ve işte onu vahyettiğimiz gibi, hıfz u ibkā eden de O’dur

ELMALILI:17:86-87/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:86-87/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:86-87/r3.claim: God’s grace to the Prophet is exceedingly great, beyond comparison with what He grants others, so he may speak with full confidence.
ELMALILI:17:86-87/r3.anchor: Diğerlerine kıyas kabul etmeyecek derecede büyüktür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r1.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r1.claim: The phrase rendered “you will find no protector against Us” can also mean finding no supporter or helper able to restore revelation to the Prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r1.anchor: onu sana geri verebilecek bir destekçi, yardımcı bulamazsın

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r2.claim: All knowledge comes from God; He could cause the Prophet and later generations to forget revelation, and no other power could protect, restore, or replace it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r2.anchor: Dilerse gönderdiği vahyi Peygamber’e ve sonra gelen nesillere unutturmak suretiyle

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r3.claim: Earlier scriptures were largely forgotten or partly altered by people, illustrating their inability to secure divine knowledge by themselves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r3.anchor: Kur’an’dan önceki kutsal kitapların büyük bir kısmı tamamen, bazısı da kısmen unutulmuş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r4.claim: God could theoretically make Muhammad forget revelation, but mercy means this will not happen in practice; people may still forget it or stray by their own choice and are responsible.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r5.claim: The verse also promises that, through God’s great favor to Muhammad, Islamic revelation will pass from generation to generation without alteration or corruption.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r5.anchor: İslâm vahyinin değişme ve bozulmaya uğramadan nesilden nesile aktarılacağı yönünde bir müjde

SAMIN-DURR:17:87/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:87/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:87/r1.claim: ‘Except as a mercy’ may be connected, included under ‘guardian’; alternatively it is disconnected, with Basrans supplying لكن and Kufans بل.
SAMIN-DURR:17:87/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { إلا رحمة }: فيها قولان، أحدهما: أنها استثناء متصل لأنها تندرج في قوله " وكيلا ".

SAMIN-DURR:17:87/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:87/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:87/r2.claim: ‘From your Lord’ may modify ‘mercy’ directly or an omitted adjective of mercy.
SAMIN-DURR:17:87/r2.anchor: و " من ربك ": يجوز أن يتعلق ب " رحمة " وأن يتعلق بمحذوف، صفة لها.

ZAJJAJ:v3p258/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p258/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p258/r3.claim: The exception is disconnected: God instead had mercy and established the revelation in the Prophet’s heart and believers’ hearts.
ZAJJAJ:v3p258/r3.anchor:
استثناء ليس من الأول، والمعنى ولكن الله رحمك فأثبت ذلك في
قلبك وقلوب المؤمنين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says God could erase the Qur'an from hearts and manuscripts, leaving the Prophet with no knowledge of the Book and no guarantor to restore it, except by God's mercy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r5.anchor: محوناه عن الصدور والمصاحف ولم نترك له أثرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari construes except God's mercy as a connected exception: divine mercy is included among the protectors against loss.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r6.anchor: جعله استثناء متصلا جعل رحمته تعالى مندرجة تحت قوله تعالى وكيلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r7.claim: Ibn al-Anbari construes the exception as discontinuous: rather, God's mercy prevents the Qur'an from being taken away.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r7.anchor: لكن رحمة من ربك تمنع من أن تسلب القرآن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya likewise takes an independent exception, meaning God's mercy keeps the revelation with the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r8.anchor: لكن رحمة من ربك تمسك ذلك عليك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r9.claim: Preservation of the Qur'an is a further divine favor after the favor of sending and teaching it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r9.anchor: وهذا امتنان من الله تعالى ببقاء القرآن محفوظا بعد المنة في تنزيله وتحفيظه

JISHUMI:v1p535/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p535/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p535/r1.claim: God sends what is most conducive to guidance and acceptance rather than what people wish for; his great favor does what best serves their religion.
JISHUMI:v1p535/r1.anchor: الآية تدل على أنه تعالى يبعث من هو أصلح، وأقرب إلى القبول، ولا يبعث مما يتمناه الخلق. ويدل على أن فضله عظيم
